$comment: WFI-6701 hot WFI storage and distribution loop twin. Expected values and pharmacopoeia limits in Maximo Monitor from the twin file; the loop sends only what it measures and the LIMS sends the sample results.

twin.name: Hot WFI storage and distribution loop WFI-6701

identification.manufacturer: Plant-built 316L loop; Alfa Laval (pump); Veolia Sievers (TOC)
identification.model: Hot WFI storage tank and recirculating distribution loop with point-of-use coolers
identification.description: Hot water-for-injection storage and distribution loop of a sterile-products plant: tank, loop pump, steam heater, 10 points of use, 2 point-of-use coolers, online conductivity and TOC
identification.tank: 10 m3 jacketed 316L storage tank, spray ball, heated hydrophobic vent filter
identification.pump: Alfa Laval LKH UltraPure hygienic centrifugal pump with a double mechanical seal (water quench), on a variable-speed drive
identification.heater: Shell-and-tube steam heater on the loop supply (plant steam on the shell side)
identification.coolers: Two point-of-use sub-loops with double tube sheet shell-and-tube coolers (chilled water on the shell side)
identification.analysers: Veolia Sievers M500 online TOC analyser and a conductivity sensor with temperature, on the loop return

loop.source: Internal diameters of ASME BPE 2 in (50.8 x 1.65 mm) and 1.5 in (38.1 x 1.65 mm) tube. Loop length, number of points of use, design supply flow and how the speed control raises the supply flow when outlets open (+0.5 m3/h per m3/h drawn): assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data

temperature.source: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) 6.10 gives constant circulation above 70 C as an example of storage and distribution that minimises microbial growth: the twin's low limit. Supply setpoint, the 75 C warning and the design temperature drop along the loop: assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data

flow.source: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) 6.9: flow turbulent, flow rate set at qualification and monitored. A minimum return velocity of about 0.9 to 1 m/s is commonly applied in design practice: assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data. Re > 4000 is the textbook threshold for fully turbulent pipe flow.

water.source: Viscosity: Vogel equation mu = A x 10^(B / (T - C)), T in K (textbook approximation, about 1 % at 80 C). Density: Tanaka et al. (2001) form, about 0.1 % at 80 C outside its 0-40 C fit range. cp of hot water: textbook value.

quality.source: USP <645> Stage 1 table (non-compensated, next lower 5 C step, no interpolation) and Stage 2 2.1 uS/cm; USP <643> 0.50 mg C/L; Ph. Eur. Water for injections: TOC max 0.5 mg/L, endotoxins < 0.25 IU/mL, microbial action level 10 CFU/100 mL. Alert levels (60 % of the conductivity limit, 250 ppb TOC): assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data; Annex 1 6.13 asks for alert levels based on the qualification data.

pump.source: Alfa Laval LKH UltraPure leaflet: 316L wetted parts, Ra <= 0.5 um, EPDM USP Class VI, -10 to +140 C, max inlet 5 bar, double mechanical seal water 0.25-0.5 l/min. Pump curve dp = dp0 x (n/n0)^2 - k x Q^2, design efficiency and quench water inlet temperature: assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data (read them from the pump's own performance curve).

cooler.source: Keeping the WFI side at a higher pressure than the cooling water, and a double tube sheet with a telltale drain between the sheets, is common design practice for WFI coolers; Annex 1 6.22 asks that leaks from heating and cooling systems be detectable. Minimum pressure difference 0.5 bar: assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data

deadleg.source: Branch length / diameter of the worst point-of-use branch, from the isometric drawings: assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data. L/D <= 2 is the dead-leg design target recommended in ASME BPE (L measured from the main pipe wall). Temperature drop alert: assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data

sanitisation.source: USP <1231>: 65-80 C most commonly used for thermal sanitisation. Annex 1 6.12: sanitisation on a predetermined schedule. Maximum time a cooled sub-loop may stay below 65 C before its hot flush: assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data

vent.source: Annex 1 6.11: prevent condensation on the tank vent filter (e.g. by heating). The heated housing must stay warmer than the tank vapour; minimum margin: assumption: typical value, replace with your loop's design documents, qualification report and operating data

toc_analyser.source: Sievers M500 specification 300 40070 Rev. D: 0.03-2,500 ppb, +-5 % or +-0.1 ppb, sample 1-95 C, 3 min online (base model 6 min), Modbus and 4-20 mA outputs.

demo.note: Demo only: the plant clock runs 60 times faster, so a production day of point-of-use draws (06:00 to 22:00) passes in 24 minutes.

groups.POU: Points of use, coolers and dead legs

points.label: Loop pump shaft power (from the drive)
Cooled draws in the last 24 h
Hours the cooled sub-loop has been below 65 °C since its last hot flush
Double tube sheet telltale wet (1 = leak)
Temperature at the worst point-of-use branch
Worst point-of-use microbial count, last sample (R2A)

limits.$comment: 70 C: Annex 1 6.10 example; 500 ppb, 0.25 EU/mL, 10 CFU/100 mL and the USP <645> table: pharmacopoeia. Other limits: assumptions to be set from the qualification data.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

heating_loss.name: Loop heating loss (steam valve or heater fouled)
heating_loss.symptoms: supply and return temperature fall below 75 C, then below 70 C; the loop is no longer self-sanitising

over_draw.name: Too many points of use open at once
over_draw.symptoms: draw grows, return flow and return velocity collapse below the qualified minimum

pump_wear.name: Loop pump impeller wear
pump_wear.symptoms: differential pressure below the pump curve at the measured flow, efficiency down

seal_wear.name: Pump mechanical seal wear (hot WFI into the quench)
seal_wear.symptoms: seal quench water outlet temperature rises

cooler_leak.name: Point-of-use cooler leak (pressure reversal, tube sheet leak)
cooler_leak.symptoms: chilled water pressure above the WFI side, telltale between the tube sheets wet

generator_upset.name: Feed or still upset (ionic and organic carry-over)
generator_upset.symptoms: conductivity above the USP <645> Stage 1 limit at the return temperature, TOC rising

biofilm_deadleg.name: Biofilm at a cooled point of use (dead leg, hot flush skipped)
biofilm_deadleg.symptoms: branch runs cold, sub-loop not hot-flushed, microbial count and endotoxin above action

vent_heater_fail.name: Vent filter heater failure
vent_heater_fail.symptoms: vent filter housing colder than the tank: condensation wets the hydrophobic membrane
